rows: Tro. By whom, Æneas? / Æne. Troilus, by Menelaus.
Æne. In all swift haste. / Tro. Come, go we then together.
Cres. Who were those went by? / Alex. Queen Hecuba and Helen.
Cres. And whither go they? / Alex. Up to the eastern tower,
In Hector's wrath. / Cres. What was his cause of anger?
They call him Ajax. / Cres. Good; and what of him?
Retorts to chiding fortune. / Ulyss. Agamemnon,
Know them from eyes of other mortals? / Agam. How!
And then to speak. / Agam. Speak frankly as the wind;
He tells thee so himself. / Æne. Trumpet, blow loud,
To overbulk us all. / Nest. Well, and how?
The vielding of her up? / Tro. Fie, fie, my brother!
The holding. / Tro. What is aught, but as ’tis valued?
Cas. [Within] Cry, Trojans, cry! / Pri. What noise? what shriek is this?
Can qualify the same? / Tro. Why, brother Hector,
Nor faint in the pursuit. / Pri. Paris, you speak
For the wide world’s revenue. / Hect. I am yours,
Or know not what we are. / Patr. I shall say so to him. [Exit.
An after-dinner's breath. / Agam. Hear you, Patroclus:
Agam. What’s his excuse? / Ulyss. He doth rely on none,
Cry“No recovery. / Agam. Let Ajax go to him.
I will be silent. / Nest. Wherefore should you so?
But be as Ajax. / Ayax. Shall I call you father?
Nest. Ay, my good son. / Dio. Be ruled by him, Lord Ajax.
Cres. Pray you, content you. / Tro. What offends you, lady?
Cres. Sir, mine own company. / Tro. You cannot shun
Cres. In that I’ll war with you. / Tro. O virtuous fight,
And sanctify the numbers. / Cres. Prophet may you be!
In most accepted pain. / Agam. Let Diomedes bear him,
To holy altars. / Achil. What, am I poor of late?
How now, Ulysses! / Ulyss. Now, great Thetis' son!
Achil. What are you reading? / Ulyss. A strange fellow here
To the first giver. / Achil. This is not strange, Ulysses.
And drave great Mars to faction. / Achil. Of this my privacy
I have strong reasons. / Ulyss. But’gainst your privacy
With one of Priam’s daughters. / Achil. Ha! known!
Be shook to air. / Achil. Shall Ajax fight with Hector?
My fame is shrewdly gored. / Patr. O, then, beware;
Par. See, ho! who is that there? / Dei. It is the Lord Æneas.
Did haunt you in the field. / Æne. Health to you, valiant sir,
We shall be much unwelcome. / Æne. That I assure you:
Than Cressid borne from Troy. / Par. There is no help;
Myself or Menelaus? / Dio. Both alike:
He shall unbolt the gates. / Tro. Trouble him not;
As infants' empty of all thought! / Cres. Good morrow, then.
Tro. I prithee now, to bed. / Cres. Are you a-weary of me?
I would not from thee. / Cres. Night hath been too brief.
You will catch cold, and curse me. / Cres. Prithee, tarry:
The Lady Cressida. / Tro, Is it so concluded?
And haste her to the purpose. / Tro. Walk into her house;
Tro. A hateful truth. / Cres. What, and from Troilus too?
Tro. From Troy and Troilus. / Cres. Is it possible?
Cres. I must then to the Grecians? / Tro. No remedy.
But yet be true. / Cres. O heavens! “be true' again!
Makes me afeard. / Cres. O heavens! you love me not.
Æne. [Within] Nay, good my lord,— / Tro. Come, kiss; and let us part.
Par. [Within] Brother Troilus! / Tro. Good brother, come you hither:
As Priam is in Ilion. / Dio. Fair Lady Cressid,
I’ll cut thy throat. / Dio. O, be not moved, Prince Troilus:
Par. Hark! Hector's trumpet. / Æne. How have we spent this morning!
And hale him hither. / Ajax. Thou, trumpet, there’s my purse.
Ulyss. No trumpet answers. / Achil. "Tis but early days.
Agam. Is this the Lady Cressid? / Dio. Even she.
Patroclus kisses you. / Men. O, this is trim!
Patr. Both take and give. / Cres. I'Il make my match to live,
Men. You fillip me o' the head. / Cres. No, I’ll be sworn.
Cres. You may. / Ulyss. I do desire it. / Cres. Why, beg, then.
Nest. A woman of quick sense. / Ulyss. Fie, fie upon her!
All. The Trojans' trumpet. / Agam. Yonder comes the troop.
Hector bade ask. / Agam. Which way would Hector have it?
The knight opposed. / Æne. If not Achilles, sir,
What is your name? / Achil. If not Achilles, nothing.
Nest. Now, Ajax, hold thine own! / Tra. Hector, thou sleep’st;
Dio. You must no more. [Trumpets cease. / Æne. Princes, enough, so please you.
Dio. As Hector pleases. / Hect. Why, then will I no more:
Cousin, all honour to thee! / Ajax. I thank thee, Hector:
What further you will do. / Hect. We ’Il answer it;
Hect. Who must we answer? / Æne. The noble Menelaus.
Must kiss their own feet. / Hect. I must not believe you:
Will one day end it. / Ulyss. So to him we leave it.
And quoted joint by joint. / Hect. Is this Achilles?
Achil. Behold thy fill. / Hect. Nay, I have done already.
Where thou wilt hit me dead ? / Achil. I tell thee, yea.
Or may I never– / Ajax. Do not chafe thee, cousin:
The Grecians' cause. / Achil. Dost thou entreat me, Hector?
To-night all friends. / Hect. Thy hand upon that match.
To bring me thither? / Ulyss. You shall command me, sir.
Patr. Here comes Thersites. / Achil. How now, thou core of envy!
Agam. We go wrong, we go wrong. / Ajax. No, yonder tis;
There, where we see the lights. / Hect. I trouble you.
Ajax. No, not a whit. / Ulyss. Here comes himself to guide you.
Men. Good night, my lord. / Hect. Good night, sweet Lord Menelaus.
I’Il keep you company. / Tro. Sweet sir, you honour me.
Hect. And so, good night. / Achil. Come, come, enter my tent.
Tro. Cressid comes forth to him. / Dio. How now, my charge!
Tro. Behold, I pray you! / Ulyss. Nay, good my lord, go off:
Tro. I pray thee, stay. / Ulyss. You have not patience; come.
I will not speak a word! / Dio. And so, good night.
Cres. Nay, but you part in anger. / Tro. Doth that grieve thee?
O wither d truth! / Ulyss. Why, how now, lord! / Tro. By Jove,
I will be patient. / Cres. Guardian!why, Greek!
You will break out. / Tro. She strokes his cheek! / Ulyss. Come, come.
Ulyss. You have sworn patience. / Tro. Fear me not, sweet lord;
Tro. O beauty! where is thy faith? / Ulyss. My lord, —
Dio. I shall have it. / Cres. What, this? / Dio. Ay, that.
Dio. I will have this: whose was it? / Cres. It is no matter.

I will not keep my word. / Dio. Why, then, farewell;
But it straight starts you. / Dio. I do not like this fooling.
Dio. Farewell till then. / Cres. Good night : I prithee, come.
Ulyss. All’s done, my lord. / Tro. It is. / Ulyss. Why stay we, then?
Was Cressid here? / Ulyss. I cannot conjure, Trojan.
Tro. She was not, sure. / Ulyss. Most sure she was.
And they’Il seem glorious. / Ulyss. O, contain yourself;
Hect. No more, I say. / Cas. Where is my brother Hector?
Cas. O, ’tis true. / Hect. Ho! bid my trumpet sound!
Unarm, sweet Hector. / Hect. Hold you still, I say;
Hect. O, 'tis fair play. / Tro. Fool’s play, by heaven, Hector.
Hect. How now! how now! / Tro. For the love of all the gods,
Hect. Fie, savage, fie! / Tro. Hector, then 'tis wars.
Fall all together. / Pri. Come, Hector, come, go back:
Therefore, come back. / Hect. Æneas is a-field;
This morning to them. / Pri. Ay, but thou shalt not go.
Cas. O Priam, vield not to him! / And. Do not, dear father.
Makes all these bodements. / Cas. O, farewell, dear Hector!
I would swim after. / Dio. Thou dost miscall retire;
And am her knight by proof. / Serv. I go, my lord. [Exit.
Ajax. Troilus! thou coward Troilus! [Exi / Dio. Ay, there, there.
Nest. So, so, we draw together. / Achil. Where is this Hector?
Dio. Troilus, I say! where’s Troilus? / Ajax. What wouldst thou?
